core_obligations: Set S = Spec(A) and reduce the statement to the structure of A: A is a finite product of local Artinian k-algebras A_i finite over k, with the corresponding decomposition Spec(A) as a disjoint union of singletons (proof lines 2020-2026).

Reduce to the case where k is algebraically closed: base change to the algebraic closure, note that flat base change preserves the global sections, choose embeddings of the residue fields kappa(s_i) into k-bar to obtain k-bar-rational points s-bar_i over s_i, and observe that the fibre of X-bar over s-bar_i is the base change of X_{s_i} (proof lines 2028-2052).

In the algebraically closed case let X_i be the inverse image of Spec(A_i) and use A_i = Gamma(X_i, O_{X_i}); the morphism X_{s_i} to X_i is a closed immersion that is a homeomorphism, so a disconnected fibre would make X_i disconnected and produce a nontrivial idempotent in the local ring A_i, a contradiction (proof lines 2054-2071).
proof_roadmap: Decompose A into local Artinian factors and read off the points of S (proof lines 2020-2026).
Descend to an algebraically closed field by flat base change (proof lines 2028-2052).
Finish by the idempotent argument in a local Artinian ring (proof lines 2054-2071).
difficulty_reason: For a proper scheme X over a field k with A = H^0(X, O_X), the lemma shows that the fibres of the canonical morphism X to Spec(A) are geometrically connected (statement lines 2012-2017). The proof first identifies A as a finite product of local Artinian k-algebras A_i finite over k, so that Spec(A) is the disjoint union of the singletons Spec(A_i) (proof lines 2020-2026), then reduces to an algebraically closed base field by base changing to the algebraic closure and using that the cohomology of the structure sheaf is preserved under flat base change (proof lines 2028-2052). In the algebraically closed case the argument is a clean local-ring computation: with X_i the inverse image of Spec(A_i), one has A_i = Gamma(X_i, O_{X_i}); if the fibre were disconnected then X_i would be disconnected, giving a nontrivial idempotent in the local ring A_i, a contradiction (proof lines 2054-2071). The claim is H2: standard inputs, but the reduction to the algebraically closed case and the idempotent argument are both written out and the local structure of A is what drives the proof.
